tasks.spec: ROLE: fix worker for the Mott booking gateway, lane 48 (restore anchor ordering). Work entirely inside your CWD; never modify anything outside it; no network, no git, no MCP/Apps/skills, no deploys. CONTEXT - decisive live probe just now against production: for store 711 on 08/07/2026, requests with time_pref='anchor=11:15 AM', time_pref='anchor=11:15 am', and time_pref='none' ALL return the identical ordering (first_start 11:00 am, then 11:15, 11:30, 11:45). The anchor branch is doing nothing - it must return slots ordered by distance from the anchor clock, so an exact 11:15 match comes FIRST. This silently degraded the pathway's 'around 2pm' route and blocks the newly built single-slot time-pick behavior. Earlier evidence (lane 38, before lanes 41-43 rewrote the ordering and out_of_hours logic) recorded anchor ordering working, so treat this as a regression in the ordering path and say in DEBUG-GW48.md which change most likely dropped it, citing the code. BASE FILE: ./deployed-bland_gateway.py is byte-equal to production image mott-lane-47. Minimal in-style diff. THE FIX: (1) In the slot-ordering function, handle a time_pref of the form 'anchor=<clock>' where the clock may be '11:15 AM', '11:15 am', '2 pm', or '14:00': parse it tolerantly, and sort the returned slots by absolute minute-distance from that clock, ties broken by earlier time; exact matches first. Keep 'latest' ordering and the plain/none ordering exactly as they are. (2) Guard against a malformed or unparseable anchor by falling back to the current default ordering rather than erroring. (3) Tests beside the existing suite: anchor 11:15 AM over a day containing 11:00/11:15/11:30/11:45 yields 11:15 first then 11:30 or 11:00; anchor '2 pm' yields 02:00 pm first; 'latest' still yields the last slot first; 'none' unchanged; malformed anchor falls back without raising. Full suite green in ./gwtest (copy of /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGW44b/gw-week-vocab-live-fix/gwtest with the fixed file installed - it is the cumulative tree; also copy any lane-46/47 test files present in /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workGW47/gw-specificity-fix/gwtest that are missing there, and report BOTH counts). (4) ./proof_anchor.py: standalone offline, exercises the ordering function directly with synthetic slots; prints 'CASE=anchor-1115 FIRST=11:15 am', 'CASE=anchor-2pm FIRST=02:00 pm', 'CASE=latest FIRST=<last slot>', 'CASE=none FIRST=<earliest slot>'. (5) DEBUG-GW48.md: the probe evidence, the regression analysis with code citation, the change, test output tails, deploy separately gated.
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 ./proof_anchor.py > proof.out 2>&1 || { echo 'FAIL: proof crashed'; tail -5 proof.out; exit 1; }; grep -q 'CASE=anchor-1115 FIRST=11:15 am' proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: anchor 11:15 not first'; cat proof.out; exit 1; }; grep -q 'CASE=anchor-2pm FIRST=02:00 pm' proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: anchor 2pm'; cat proof.out; exit 1; }; grep -qE 'CASE=latest FIRST=' proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: latest case missing'; exit 1; }; grep -qE 'CASE=none FIRST=' proof.out || { echo 'FAIL: none case missing'; exit 1; }; cd gwtest && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q > ../pytest.out 2>&1; rc=$?; cd ..; summary=$(tail -1 pytest.out); [ $rc -eq 0 ] || { echo "FAIL: suite red: $summary"; tail -10 pytest.out; exit 1; }; n=$(echo "$summary" | grep -oE '^[0-9]+'); [ "$n" -ge 85 ] || { echo "FAIL: only $n tests ran; cumulative suite is >=85"; exit 1; }; grep -qi 'anchor' DEBUG-GW48.md || { echo 'FAIL: DEBUG lacks the anchor analysis'; exit 1; }; echo "PASS: anchor ordering restored - $summary"
tasks.verified: Anchor-ordered searches once again put the nearest slot to the requested clock first (exact match first), with latest/none ordering unchanged and the full cumulative suite green - the regression that silently flattened anchor ordering is closed.
